title: Elon Musk's Flying Roadster: How the Rocket Car Really Works

value.name: tesla_roadster_fan_and_rocket_layout
simplified: The model represents the Tesla Roadster-style electric prototype described in the research, not a confirmed production vehicle.

Overall car dimensions, battery size, motor size, fan size, tank size and internal positions are estimated for a clear explainer layout because Tesla has not published a complete engineering blueprint.
The car is shown about 4.7 metres long, 2.0 metres wide and 1.2 metres tall.
The battery, power electronics and electric motors are shown as separate simplified blocks.
The suction system is represented by four fan modules and a continuous underbody seal. The real system is described by Tesla as a multi-mode fan and ground-sealing system.

The Rocket version is represented with two pressure-tank blocks and four visible thruster groups. These stand for a larger distributed cold-gas-thruster array; the exact internal layout is not publicly documented here.
The fan system creates downforce by lowering pressure beneath the car. It does not provide free-flight lift.
The thruster sections show the general direction of cold gas leaving the vehicle. No manufacturing or nozzle-construction detail is included.
The Rocket version is treated as a one-seat prototype configuration, while the normal electric-car layout retains a conventional cabin.
Exact production status, certification, repeated-flight capability and final road equipment remain unresolved in the supplied research.

value.name: Tesla Roadster: drive, suction, and rocket prototype
simplified: The model represents the announced Rocket configuration, with the ordinary electric-car systems shown underneath.

Tesla publishes the functions of the Roadster systems but not a complete production dimension drawing, so the 4.8 m overall length and other dimensions are explanatory estimates based on sports-car proportions.
The suction system is simplified into a flat underbody plenum, sealing skirt, and two visible fan units. The real fan count, ducting, and skirt geometry have not been fully published.

The Rocket version is shown with a simplified central pressure-tank system and perimeter thruster pods. Tesla says the Rocket has one seat and thrusters around the vehicle, but does not publish a complete engineering layout.

The model shows general operation only: battery power drives motors and wheels, fans create downforce by lowering pressure underneath, and compressed gas thrusters provide brief control or lift. It is not a manufacturing drawing.
The three trims are not separate full cars in this model. Performance keeps the EV and suction hardware; Thrust adds rear thrusters; Rocket adds the larger tank and perimeter thrusters.
The flying demonstration was a staged prototype event. The Rocket trim is listed by Tesla as not approved for public road use.

value.name: Tesla Rocket Roadster
simplified: The dimensions are approximate explanatory proportions, not Tesla production drawings; Tesla has not published complete Rocket-version dimensions.
The model combines the normal electric Roadster layout, the suction-fan system, and the Rocket trim's compressed-gas hardware in one exploded view.
The battery, motors, wheels and power electronics are shown as representative components; exact motor and battery packaging is not publicly specified.
The suction system is simplified into one underbody fan module and one sealing skirt.
The perimeter thrusters are represented as a ten-bay ring, matching Tesla's stated Rocket concept without showing manufacturing detail.
The tank shape, capacity and pressure are not specified because complete public engineering data is unavailable.
The flying demonstration was a prototype-style demonstration, not proof of a certified, repeatable public-road flying car.

value.name: Tesla Rocket Roadster
simplified: The exact production dimensions, mass, battery layout, tank geometry, fan size, and thruster placement have not been fully published; the dimensions shown are explanatory estimates based on a compact two-seat electric sports car.
This blueprint represents the Rocket configuration: one seat, a rear pressure tank, an additional tank in the passenger area, suction fans and perimeter cold-gas thrusters.
The 10 thrusters are grouped into three visual modules rather than modeled individually.
The fan rotors, sealing skirt, and thruster directions are diagrammatic; the builders keep every part aligned along +X.
The wheel material uses plastic_dark because rubber_black is not an allowed material. It represents a dark tire visually, not the tire's literal material.
The Rocket version is described by Tesla as not approved for public-road use. The flying demonstration should be treated as a prototype demonstration, not proof of a certified flying car.
